result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Answer A cuts the welcome to two quick actions. It splits the rest into a tiered checklist that stays in the app, labels team invites, accounting and cycle counts as later steps, and explains each choice. It loses some credit because approval rules still sit before the first order, and it says steps appear when useful even though they all show in the checklist. Answer B fixes the order and groups the steps, but it keeps all nine as a single required wizard and gives only a generic 'return later' note for anything put off. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Answer B cuts the first-run modal to two actions and moves the rest to a persistent checklist, with a 'Later' tier for team invites, accounting and cycle counts. It explains each change and flags its assumptions. It still puts approval rules before the first order, which the rubric wanted deferred. Answer A regroups and reorders the same nine steps without deferring anything, so it adds headings but leaves the new admin with the same workload.
